title: Dragon Forge: Chromatic Armor Shader
description: A translucent dragon floats above a carbon fibre platform. The user clicks body regions of the dragon to progressively apply a custom carbon fibre armor shader that spreads outward from each click point with a chromatic dispersion edge effect. A slider controls the dispersion intensity along armor boundaries.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive dragon armor forging scene. Load DragonDispersion.glb as the central dragon model and CarbonFibre.glb as a flat platform beneath it. Camera: perspective at position (0, 2, 5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls enabled. Lighting: one directional light from upper-right, one ambient light, and one point light beneath the dragon casting upward glow. For the dragon, write a custom ShaderMaterial with vertex and fragment shaders. The vertex shader passes world-space position and UV to the fragment. The fragment shader blends between two states: a base translucent glass-like dispersion look (using a simplified chromatic aberration effect that offsets RGB channels based on view angle via dot(normal, viewDir)) and an armored state that samples a carbon fibre texture extracted from the CarbonFibre model's material (or use its diffuse map as a tiling pattern). Maintain a uniform array of up to 6 click points in world space and a uniform radius for each. In the fragment shader, for each click point, calculate distance from the fragment world position; if within radius, blend toward the carbon fibre armored look. At the boundary edge, amplify the chromatic dispersion effect to create a glowing prismatic seam. Interactions: (1) User clicks on the dragon via raycasting to place armor seed points (max 6). (2) Each click triggers an animation that expands that point's radius from 0 to 0.8 over one second using requestAnimationFrame. (3) A slider labeled 'Dispersion Intensity' (range 0-2, default 0.5) controls the chromatic offset strength at armor edges. (4) A reset button clears all armor points. (5) The dragon slowly rotates on its Y-axis. Display a small instruction overlay in the top-left corner. The platform from CarbonFibre should sit at y=-1 with a subtle reflective floor shader using the same carbon fibre pattern.
